source-integrity.provenance: SEC Q2 filing anchors financial state; issuer milestone is separated from independent cash-use and valuation reporting
source-integrity.freshness: Q2 filing August 7, execution reporting August 10, valuation September 9
source-integrity.duplicateOriginCollapse: repeated Scout copies are not independent corroboration
source-integrity.sourceIndependence: SEC and issuer claims are not treated as independent; external reporting is separately identified
source-integrity.rawDerivedConsistency: large liquidity coexists with operating losses, cash use and equity financing; pilot milestones are not commercial revenue proof

company-underwriting.financialOperatingTrajectory: Pre-commercial profile with significant losses and cash use offset by substantial liquidity.
company-underwriting.balanceSheet: Liquidity is substantial but financing history is equity-heavy, making dilution material.
company-underwriting.customersContracts: Deployment activity supports demand thesis but current evidence does not establish operating Aurora revenue or fleet economics.
company-underwriting.governanceCapitalAllocation: Capital access is strong while capital discipline remains unproven before commercial operation.
company-underwriting.pricingPowerConcentration: Mission-critical firm power may support pricing, but realized fleet margin evidence does not yet exist.
company-underwriting.catalysts: Aurora-INL licensing, construction, commissioning and first commercial power operation.

thesisQuality.basis: Durable firm-power problem and real milestones, but commercial economics and fleet adoption remain unproven.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Large liquidity supports execution, but company remains loss-making and pre-commercial with equity-funded expansion.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: Independent valuation reporting implies aggressive future outcomes despite no meaningful commercial reactor revenue.

catalystScore.basis: Concrete safety/deployment progress creates identifiable milestones, though commercial authorization remains ahead.

governancePower.basis: Management secured capital and advanced deployment, but heavy equity issuance and unproven economics keep evidence mixed.

alignment2036.basis: Firm low-carbon power, nuclear fuel and isotope capabilities address durable electricity and strategic infrastructure needs.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Powerhouses, fuel/recycling and isotopes provide related demand channels, but cross-leverage is not proven at scale.

bottleneckControl.basis: Licensing, fuel and deployment know-how are scarce, but system-critical commercial control is not yet demonstrated.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Firm-power need is durable, while thesis remains dependent on licensing, construction and nuclear economics.

substitutionResilience.basis: Compact nuclear differentiation exists, but gas, renewables/storage, grid expansion and competing reactors remain substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Fuel and nuclear-component dependencies remain material; tested multi-source resilience is not established.

pricingPower.basis: Future mission-critical power may support value capture, but realized commercial fleet pricing evidence is absent.

riskEvidence.basis: Pre-commercial licensing/construction risk, fuel dependencies, equity issuance and demanding valuation create very high risk.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Current SEC financials and deployment evidence are strong; commercial unit economics and fleet margins remain unknown.

scoreRecord.thesis: Oklo has strong liquidity and advanced-nuclear execution progress against durable firm-power need, but value depends on converting milestones into commercial economics without excessive dilution.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: Licensing or first-of-a-kind economics can slip while equity-funded spending continues.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Further Aurora-INL authorization/construction progress toward commercial operation.

contradictions.claim: Strong liquidity versus heavy dilution and continuing losses.
contradictions.resolution: Both retained; runway is strong but equity-funded and does not prove economics.

unknowns.item: Commercial unit economics, realized customer revenue, final licensing timing and tested fuel redundancy remain unproven.
